name: 1736 Prairie Avenue — the Ingraham/McBirney house, its veranda front from the c. 1890 photograph, K01 frontage assembly

grade.why: Pictured: a picture on the Images tab shows it.

documented_range.note: The draft claims the 1904 target and no more: the 1911 sheet draws the building and the T-1840 census rules it present in 1904 (present_as_mapped). THE HOUSE'S DATE AND ITS MANSARD'S (T-2962): the house was 'completed in 1864' for Granville S. Ingraham (glessner_blog_2020_07_early_history_prairie_iv) — or, as the Prairie library reads an 1875 permit for this lot, built for Gen. Henry Strong in 1875 (T-3037; the structure's `built` carries both) — and that post's author judges the mansard 'may well have been a later addition' to an Italianate house of the Civil War years; nothing read here dates the mansard, and the Keith house at 1900 Prairie had its mansard added in the 1880s (glessner_blog_2014_11_elbridge_keith_house), so a later mansard is the street's own pattern, not a proof for this house. For this phase the question is bounded either way: the c. 1890 photograph (earliest 1885) shows the mansard and the veranda front, and the 1911 sheet draws the mansard's curb and prints the house '3B', so the house as built here stood from at least the late 1880s to 1911. The range keeps to the 1904 target because only the front is seen in c. 1890; the flank's bays are the 1911 sheet's. When the house lost the mansard or was demolished is not read.

placement.position_note: The main body's rear south corner: the draft's frame point u 0.00, v -0.75 (draft position note: the rear corner of the main body's rectangle, lot frame u 22.750, v -2.125 m from the middle of the rear lot line, through the T-1250 fit of the sheet, whose own fit residual, 3.08 m RMS on its control crossings, is all that is claimed; rotation -0.618 degrees turns the plan's u axis onto the lot's own rear-to-street line). Moved by T-2933 from the corner of the draft's fitted strip to the corner of the sheet's own plan: the trace's south wall runs at draft v -0.71 to -0.85 from the rear to the front, so -0.75.

footprint.note: The main body read off the 1911 sheet's trace (s20fp-1736-b1 p3) in the draft's lot frame: the rear wall at u -0.05 to 0.10, the front at 23.27 to 23.36, the south wall at v -0.71 to -0.85 and the north at 5.88 to 6.26 (its jogs are the sheet's printed figures, not walls), so 23.3 m deep and 6.75 m along the street. The photograph's front reads 216 px across at 32 px/m through its camera, 6.75 m. The south wall's three canted bays (u 3.37-6.01 frame, 9.42-12.75 brick and 15.97-19.17 frame, about 0.85 m out) are K08's, on the wall (T-2962, `bays`); the veranda (the sheet's frame porch p1/p2, 1.8 m deep the front's width) is the entrance kit's.

stories.note: Two storeys over a raised basement under a mansard, the attic storey in the roof: the photograph shows two rows of windows on the front under one cornice and the mansard with its dormers above it. The 1911 sheet's '3B' counts the mansard storey (T-2933). T-2995: on the north wall, the rear and the 18th Street wall behind the brick bay the third storey is a straight brick storey, not the mansard's (roof_form), as the sheet's three wall figures to a wall and its curb line say.

construction.note: The 1911 sheet colours the building pink, its brick ('3B brick dwelling'); the photograph shows the walls light, so painted (wall_finish).

wall_finish.note: The walls PAINTED over their brick, the paint opaque (T-2933: K01's paint otherwise tints the brick's map, and no tint of the buff brick is as light as this): the photograph shows them nearly as light as its sky against the dark sash, hoods and cornice shadow. The tone is read, the colour is not (the print is monochrome): a pale stone colour is RECONSTRUCTED.

principal_floor_m.note: The veranda's deck at the principal floor, its front edge at y 452 px through the camera (data/reference_views/house_1736_prairie/mcbirney_c1890_photo.json), 1.85 m over grade at the deck's face; the raised basement's lights show under it.

storey_heights_m.note: The bracketed cornice's soffit at y 194 px on the front through the camera, 9.9 m over grade, less the 1.85 m floor: 8.05 m for two storeys. The split puts the second floor 0.55 m under the upper windows' sills (y 300 px, 6.6 m); the principal storey is the taller, as the photograph's long openings behind the veranda say.

service_wall_brick.note: RECONSTRUCTED: the K03 common brick panel 1620 wears; painted over by wall_finish.

street_front_trim.note: RECONSTRUCTED: the principal storey's heads are hidden under the veranda's frieze, so the K01 flat lintel; the side and rear walls' segmental brick heads, as 1620's.

street_front_round_heads.note: T-2960: the upper storey's three street windows read off the photograph at 32 px/m: each light's head a segmental arch rising about 7 px (0.22 m) from rounded springs to its crown over a 28 px (0.95 m) span, so 0.22 of the span, and over each a flat moulded cornice hood about 54 px (1.7 m) across, its underside about 2 px over the crown, with a drop under each end standing just outside the jambs about 11 px (0.35 m) deep: the ends that turn down. Built as K09's cornice hood on its two scrolled consoles over a segmental hole cut to that rise, the block 0.25 m past each jamb so that with its cornice's 0.115 m return the hood stands about 1.7 m across. The hood's profile and the consoles' carving are the kit's (the print is too small to read them); a print at higher resolution would set both.

wall_head.note: A bracketed cornice under the mansard: the photograph's dark band of brackets across the front at y 186-196 px. Its profile and bracket spacing are not read; K10's bracketed timber cornice, round all four walls.

roof_form.note: A mansard: the photograph shows a steep lower slope from the cornice to a curb with round-headed dormers in it on the street face; the register's 'bounded mansard/attic treatment'. Its date is argued in the phase's documented_range (T-2962): it stood from at least the late 1880s to 1911, its first date unread. THE CURB ON THE SHEET runs along the street front about 1.2 m inside it and along the 18th Street wall about 1.0 m inside it from the front back only to the brick bay (u about 9.9), where it turns down into the bay's rear cheek; no dashed line is drawn along the north wall or over the rear 9.9 m. The sheet prints '12 12 8' against the north wall near u 14-17 and '14 12 12' against the south wall near u 13-15 (wall thicknesses in inches, storey by storey, as T-2934 read '12 12' on 1726 and 1730); whether those figures begin at the basement is not settled here, so they do not yet say whether the north side and the rear rise as a straight brick third storey. THE CURB ON THE SHEET, RULED (T-2995). The sheet's key draws a mansard roof as a dashed line inside the building's outline, and on 1736 that line runs about 1.2 m inside the street front and about 1.0 m inside the 18th Street wall from the front back to the brick bay (u about 9.9), where it turns down into the bay's rear cheek; none is drawn along the north wall or over the rear 9.9 m. The figures against the walls are, by the same key ('Figures 20, 16, 12, 8 indicate thickness of wall in inches'), one wall thickness to a storey, and each wall carries three: '12 12 8' on the north (u about 14-17) and '14 12 12' on the south (u about 13-15), the three storeys of the building's '3B' over its basement. So the north wall stands brick, 8 inches thick, through the third storey, and the rear, which the line leaves out as it leaves out the north, is ruled the same: the mansard stands on the street front and on the 18th Street wall forward of the brick bay, and the north side, the rear and the 18th Street wall behind the bay rise as a straight brick third storey (the service side). Built: K05's mansard on the street front and the south face from u 9.9 (`mansard.straight`), the straight walls carried up from the eave as coped brick parapets 0.45 m over the curb, and where the two mansard faces end (the street front's at the north wall, the south face at u 9.9) their section is closed in the wall's brick.

entrance_kit.note: The photograph's veranda (T-2933), the 1911 sheet's frame porch (s20fp-1736-b1 p1/p2) 1.8 m deep across the whole front: a deck at the principal floor (the stoop's landing and K07's terraces either side of it, south to the front's corner and north to its end), a turned balustrade along its front, four slender posts (x 337, 412, 484 and 535 px at the deck's front through the camera, 34 px/m there: v 0.15, 2.85, 4.9 and 6.6 m), a beam and a deep frieze over them (its soffit y 335 px, 5.25 m over grade, and its fascia y 300 px, about 1 m deep with the roof edge), and a low hipped roof from the wall. The stair rises at the north end between the last two posts (stoop_v_m 5.65 for the 1.2 m flight), straight out toward the walk, as the photograph draws its cheeks. front_yard_m is the street grid's: the front stands 9.07 m behind the Prairie Avenue street line (the draft's street_u 32.374 less the 23.3 m body) and the walk begins 1 ft further out. T-2960: the deck stands open beneath, as the photograph shows it: each post runs on down past the deck to grade (the posts' lower lengths stand at the same x 337-535 px, a pier under each), and between them the raised basement's front reads dark; built as K07's veranda `open_under`, the deck's skirt 0.2 m deep (the deck's front edge, y 450-457 px, 7 px at 34 px/m) and the void behind it set 0.5 m back (RECONSTRUCTED: how far back the basement's front stands under the deck is not seen). The balustrade is painted timber with the walls, a top rail at y 425 px (0.8 m over the deck) and slender balusters at about 0.14 m (the print shows the infill as a light pierced band, too small to read its pattern; RECONSTRUCTED). The frieze is one beam and the posts are plain square sections. T-2961: the roof's slope. In the print the band over the posts is a lit strip about 5 px deep along its foot (y 331-336, 0.15 m at 34 px/m) under a darker, textured band (y 306-331) that runs up to the upper wall, whose sills show over it at y 300-304. The strip is the fascia and the band the roof itself: a slope rising away from the camera shows from the walk whenever it rises steeper than the eye's line to it, and T-2933's (0.35 m over the roof's 2 m) rose at about the line's own 0.17, so it was seen edge-on and the beam's 0.6 m face stood where the print draws roof. Built now as the print draws it: the beam 0.1 m deep under a 0.08 m roof edge, 5.25-5.43 m over grade (y 336-330 px through the camera), and the roof rising 1.0 m to the wall, its ridge there at 6.43 m (y 306 px at the wall's 28.25 m), under the upper sills at 6.6. The texture (shingles or standing seams) is not readable at this scale and is the roof's own covering; nor is what the darker mark in the band over three of the posts is (x 340, 412 and 485 px against the posts' 337, 412 and 484), and nothing is built for it. The pitch is read through the camera's distance, like every height here (RECONSTRUCTED within it: L-k01-1736-mcbirney-veranda-2933).

Its top reads at y 501 px from x 212 to 440 (0.74 m) and at y 491 px from x 476 to 628 (0.95 m); the step lies behind the street tree at x 456-472, s 4.2-4.6 m on the line, built at 4.3. The taller run ends at x 628 px, s 7.79, which is where the 1904 parcel's north lot line (data/street_grid/1904.json prairie_1736) meets the street line in this frame: the photograph and the parcel agree there without being fitted to each other. The line is the street grid's: the front stands 9.07 m behind it, and the lot runs s -0.65 to 7.79 along it (the parcel's corners taken into the house's frame). The wall's material is the Glessner House Museum's 2015 photograph of the McBirney curbstone still in place on the lot line (Prairie library a16-ghm-blog-1736-mcbirney-curbstone-2015, read 2026-10-21 from the image store's copy, sha256 e00ecb6a…; link only, so forms only are read): squared limestone blocks with a chamfered top arris, stepping up at one block, as the c. 1890 wall steps up. The wall reads continuous across the stair's line in the print (x 490-540 and 562-600 px), so no opening is cut; whatever gave onto the walk is hidden behind the tree or the ice wagon, and nothing is built for it. Nothing turns the 18th Street corner: no picture shows a return. The pier is the stair's: at the foot of its south cheek, whose top rakes down to it, x 475-507 px, its top at y 462, 1.55 m over grade at the foot's distance (and 1.56 m were it on the street line, so the height does not rest on where it stands); its lower part is hidden behind the street wall. RECONSTRUCTED: the wall's thickness (0.35 m) and the chamfer (0.06 m), the pier's section (0.6 m under a 0.06 m cap; the print's 32 px include its cap's shadow), and that the stone is limestone in c. 1890 as in 2015 (L-k01-1736-mcbirney-veranda-2933). T-3205 (the owner: some fronts 'cant enter'): the wall is not continuous at the step. Read again, the low run's top ends at the street tree's edge (x 440 px, s 3.86), the taller run starts behind the stair's pier (x 477-490, s 4.6-4.95), and between them, at x 460-477 (s 4.3-4.6), the print shows the stone at grade, not a wall's top (its top line at y 527 against the ground's 536). That gap is the walk's opening; its two edges are hidden by the tree and the pier, so it is built s 3.9-4.9, 1.0 m, the most the print allows, and the low run ends there instead of at 4.3. The ground-level stone in the gap (a sill, or a step's top) is not built. RECONSTRUCTED: the opening's two edges (liberty L-k14-walks-1700-block-3205).

mansard.note: The mansard read off the photograph through the camera: its curb at y 103 px, 12.7 m over grade, 2.7 m over the eave; its lower faces near upright and straight. Two round-headed dormers on the street face, their lights at x 383-398 and 478-493 px (v 2.12 and 5.18 m at the mansard's face), sills at y 178 px and round heads at y 120 px. The one on the south face over 18th Street (u 15.5) is RECONSTRUCTED: no picture sees that face; T-2995 took away the second, at u 8.0, since the sheet stands no mansard behind the brick bay. The mansard's EXTENT is the 1911 sheet's (roof_form, T-2995): the street front, and the south face from u 9.9 to the front; the north wall, the rear and the south wall behind the bay are straight (`straight`), their parapets 0.45 m over the curb (RECONSTRUCTED: the sheet gives no height; 0.45 m is K05's 0.3 m least upstand over the upper deck's covering at the parapet's inner face, with room). No picture sees those walls, so their third storey is built blank, as the north wall's lower storeys are; a window there is unread, not absent.

bays.note: T-2962: the 18th Street wall's three projections read off the 1911 sheet's raster (trace s20fp-1736-b1's outline, pixels x 2738-3049, y 6045-6062) in the record's frame, the wall at v 0 and each about 0.85 m out, every one drawn CANTED, its face shorter than its foot. REAR: yellow, frame, u 3.37-6.01 at the wall, its face 3.94-5.36. MIDDLE: pink, brick, u 9.42-12.75 at the wall, its face 9.93-12.21; the mansard's dashed curb turns down into its rear cheek, so it rises under the roof. FRONT: yellow, frame, u 15.97-19.17 at the wall, its face 16.48-18.51; the trace's rule read it as a frame porch (p4), but the sheet draws it in solid lines, closed and canted like the rear one, not in a porch's dashes, so it is a frame bay. RECONSTRUCTED: the heights, the one window a storey on each face, the blank cheeks, the sash, the roofs, and the frame bays' boards in K08's dark painted timber against the painted brick (the kit's colour, as 1626's and 1730's frame bays wear it; the sheet gives fabric, not paint). built.note: THE SOURCES DISAGREE AND THIS RECORD DOES NOT CHOOSE. The Glessner House Museum's post has the large brick house at 1736 'completed in 1864' for Granville S. Ingraham (glessner_blog_2020_07_early_history_prairie_iv). The Tribune of 8 August 1875, as the Prairie library read it, prints a permit to Gen. Henry Strong for a two-storey-and-basement brick house 23 feet wide at old 882 Prairie, this lot, and chicagology gives the house a life span of 1875-1912; Strong sold the improved lot to Hugh McBirney in December 1880 (chicagology_1736_prairie_page). So the house McBirney lived in may be Ingraham's of 1864 or Strong's of 1875. Inferred, because the permit is not re-read here and neither account names the other. Either way it stood by about 1890, when it was photographed (glessner_blog_1736_mcbirney_c1890_photo), and in 1893, when Rand McNally's bird's-eye guide drew it (Prairie library st-randmcnally-1893-p233-west-1700-1800).

research_note: T-2933 (piece 1 of T-1874) refines the district draft (T-2334) in place under the same id from the c. 1890 photograph of the house the Glessner House Museum reproduces (glessner_blog_1736_mcbirney_c1890_photo), read against the 1911 Sanborn sheet 20, which controls the plan. The draft's 5.5 m strip becomes the sheet's own main body, 23.3 m deep and 6.75 m along the street, on K01: two storeys over a raised basement under a slated mansard with two round-headed dormers on the street face, a bracketed cornice, three arched upper windows, and the photograph's timber veranda the front's whole width (the sheet's frame porch) on K07's terrace, with its stair at the north end. The camera is solved into data/reference_views/house_1736_prairie/mcbirney_c1890_photo.json; what the picture still shows differently is on its match record. T-2960 (piece 1 of T-2935) builds the upper windows' segmental heads under K09 cornice hoods on consoles, and the veranda's deck open beneath on its posts carried to grade, in painted timber with its balustrade. The street wall and the set-back front left of the house are T-2961's; T-2962 builds the 18th Street wall's three canted bays off the sheet (a frame bay, the brick bay and a frame bay where the draft read a side porch) and argues the mansard's date (roof_form); T-2995 rules the roof behind the sheet's curb and builds it: the mansard on the street front and the south face forward of the brick bay, the north side, the rear and the south wall behind the bay a straight brick third storey (roof_form, `mansard.straight`), and refines the coach house onto K12. docs/RESEARCH/k01-1736-mcbirney-2933/README.md.
